title: Applied ML Eval Harness + Prompt Sets + Onboarding + Guardrails + Quantization + Regression Playbook
author: Ariana Chen
body:
Summary

This playbook consolidates Redwood's applied-ML and evaluation practices for: the eval-harness, prompt set & benchmark management, model onboarding, quality guardrails, quantization profiles, and regression triage. It is intended for ML Engineers, Applied ML, and SREs involved in shipping model changes to production inference.

Goals

- Provide a single, repeatable onboarding path for new models.
- Standardize prompt sets and benchmarks for cross-model comparisons.
- Define quality gate metrics and acceptable regressions.
- Provide quantization guidance and safe rollout patterns.
- Document a fast, repeatable regression triage process.

Owners and Contacts

- Primary owner: Applied ML Team (engineering)
- Oncall for regressions: eng-sre (pager: #applied-ml-regressions)
- Eval-harness engineering lead: Diego Morales
- Product lead (feature impacts): Priya Nair

High-level workflow (one-line)

Model candidate -> Eval-harness onboarding -> Prompt set benchmarking -> Quality guardrail checks -> Quantization profile testing -> Canary rollout -> Regression triage (if needed) -> Promote to stable.

1) Eval-harness onboarding checklist

Purpose: Ensure models are instrumented in the eval harness with reproducible metrics, CI integration, and baseline comparisons.

Mandatory steps:

1.1 Create a model entry in the model registry with tags: architecture, family, size, training_data_tag, provenance, and model_sha.

1.2 Add model to eval-harness config (eval_config/<model-name>.yaml): include model_id, endpoint (stub for attended testing), batch profile, max_seq_length, and tokenization settings.

1.3 Provide reference generation seeds and deterministic sampling settings for unit tests (temperature=0.0 / top_p=1.0 for deterministic tests where applicable).

1.4 Attach at least three canonical prompt sets from the Prompt Catalog (see section 2).

1.5 Run the baseline eval job locally and in CI (action: .github/workflows/eval-harness.yml). Collect: latency P50/P95/P99, tokens/sec, mean_logprob, and primary quality metrics for each prompt set.

Acceptance criteria (to add to PR):

- Latency should be within 15% of expected for family/size baseline.
- Quality metrics must not be >5% worse than current family baseline on primary benchmarks (unless approved by product).
- Regression ticket created if any guardrail metric fails hard thresholds (see section 4).

2) Prompt sets and benchmarks (management)

Purpose: Maintain a canonical library of prompts and expected outputs to measure quality/regressions.

Structure and metadata for each prompt set (stored in /prompt-sets):

- id (short-dash-name)
- owner_team
- domain (e.g., summarization, Q&A, code, math, conversational)
- size (number of examples)
- creation_date and last_reviewed
- tags: [difficulty, hallucination-risk, safety-sensitive]
- evaluation-metric (e.g., ROUGE-L, Exact Match, S-BERT cosine, human-rate)

Best practices:

- Keep prompt sets balanced by difficulty and representative of customer workloads.
- Include edge cases and adversarial examples at ~10-20% of the set.
- For safety-sensitive domains include manual human labels and expected safe responses.

Benchmarking cadence and CI:

- Nightly runs: quick smoke on small prompt subsets.
- Weekly runs: full coverage for actively used models.
- Release runs: full suite with human-in-the-loop checks for safety-sensitive prompt sets.

3) Model onboarding guide (step-by-step)

Step 1: Pre-onboarding (owner: model owner)

- Confirm license and provenance. Fill model registry entry.
- Provide a short README with intended capabilities and known limitations.

Step 2: Local eval + profiling (owner: eval-harness engineer)

- Run eval-harness locally with the sample prompt sets. Collect perf counters: mem_peak, kv_cache_usage, tokens/sec.
- Produce performance profile and recommended batch_size/sequence truncation for production.

Step 3: Quantization dry-run (owner: quantization SME)

- Test recommended quantization recipes (INT8, FP16->INT8, and 4-bit recipes where supported) against a 200-example prompt subset.
- Measure quality delta and latency improvement.

Step 4: Staging canary (owner: infra/platform)

- Deploy model to staging with 2% traffic and full telemetry: latency, errors, hallucination-rate, and human_in_loop flags.
- Observe for minimum of 48 hours or 20k requests, whichever is larger.

Step 5: Production ramp (owner: platform/product)

- Ramp schedule (default): 2% -> 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with at least 24 hours between steps and metric checks at each stage.
- Automations: automatic rollback on hard guardrail failures (see section 4).

4) Quality guardrails and metrics

Core quantitative metrics (computed per prompt-set and aggregated):

- Primary quality metric: depends on domain (e.g., ROUGE-L for summarization, Exact Match/F1 for QA, S-BERT sim for semantic similarity).
- Hallucination rate: % of responses with fabricated facts (estimated via topic-specific QA checks and heuristics).
- Safety violations: % of responses flagged by safety classifiers.
- Latency P95 and Error rate (5xx/4xx) for the model endpoint.
- Mean token log-prob and calibration drift vs baseline.

Thresholds (example defaults)

- Soft guardrail: primary metric drop <= 3% vs baseline - requires a cross-functional review.
- Hard guardrail: primary metric drop > 7% OR hallucination rate increase > 2x OR safety violations > 0.5% OR latency P95 increase > 30% - automatic rollback and regression process.

Escalation matrix

- Soft fail: notify owner, create review ticket, schedule 24h deep-dive.
- Hard fail: page oncall SRE and product lead, initiate regression triage (see section 6).

5) Quantization profiles and guidance

Profiles are recorded per model in model-registry under quantization_profile (human-readable tag). Each profile must include: recommended bits (8/4), expected perf uplift (%), expected quality delta (primary metric), and recommended fallback.

Recommended process:

- Start with conservative INT8 calibration (per-channel where supported).
- Measure quality delta on the validation prompt subset; if primary metric drop <= 1.5% prefer INT8.
- For aggressive 4-bit recipes, perform human evaluation on a 500-example sample and require product sign-off if quality delta > 0.5%.
- Provide a fallback path: if production quality metrics degrade beyond soft guardrail, automatically fall back to the previous quantization profile or FP16.

Quantization testing checklist:

- Accuracy: report primary metric delta and hallucination delta.
- Determinism: check generation sampling behavior for seeded deterministic tasks.
- Memory & throughput: report memory reduction and tokens/sec uplift.
- Failure modes: list observed tokenization mismatches and out-of-vocab artifacts.

6) Regression triage playbook (runbook)

Purpose: Rapidly identify, mitigate, and resolve quality or performance regressions detected in CI, nightly runs, or production.

6.1 Initial detection

- Source of signal: CI fail, nightly alert, canary guardrail, or customer report.
- Triage owner: person oncall for applied-ml (check rotations).

6.2 Immediate mitigation (first 30 min)

- If production: reduce traffic to affected model by 50% and initiate rollback to last stable model/quantization profile.
- If canary: freeze rollout and revert canary changes.
- Create a high-priority incident ticket and tag with labels: regression, model-id, prompt-set, and impact.

6.3 Data collection (30-120 min)

- Gather: failing prompt examples, full metric diffs (per-prompt-set), recent deployment manifest, quantization profile, and hardware allocation.
- Run difference-of-outputs diff on suspect prompt sets. Store artifacts in the incident ticket (links to S3 and eval-harness job run).

6.4 Root cause analysis (2-24 hours)

- Hypotheses checklist: model weights change, quantization delta, tokenization mismatch, prompt template change, routing to different model variant, infra degradation, or latent data drift.
- Assign owners: model code, quantization, infra, and product.

6.5 Resolution and verification

- If fix is code/config: push patch to staging and run full eval-harness suite.
- If rollback: validate the rollback by re-running failing prompt sets and monitoring for recurrence for 24-72 hours.

- Add regression postmortem with timeline, root cause, corrective actions, and action owners.

6.6 Post-incident actions (within 7 days)

- Update prompt sets or add synthetic examples for the failure mode.
- If required, tighten guardrails or adjust quantization profiles.
- Schedule a cross-functional review if outage impact > 1% of customer traffic.

7) CI, reporting, and dashboards

- CI integration: every model-change PR must run quick eval-harness smoke tests. Merged PRs trigger nightly full-suite runs.
- Dashboards: per-model dashboard with token-level cost, latency P95, primary quality metric time-series, hallucination-rate, and safety flags.

- Alerts: configured for soft guardrail drift (warn) and hard guardrail breach (page).

8) Templates and artifacts

Below are example artifacts to attach to every model onboarding PR:

- eval-harness run URL and run id
- prompt-set list with owners and sample failing examples (if any)
- quantization_profile_summary.txt with recommended profile and measured deltas
- performance_profile.json (JSON blob with mem_peak, tokens/sec, latency percentiles)
- rollout_plan.md with ramp schedule and automation hooks

9) FAQ and common pitfalls

Q: My nightly tests show a 2% drop in ROUGE after quantization - OK to proceed?
A: 2% is within soft guardrail; schedule a review with product and evaluate a larger human sample before full rollout.

Q: Hallucination heuristics are noisy - how do we trust them?
A: Use heuristics as early warning; always validate with a human-in-the-loop for safety-sensitive prompt sets and rely on multiple signals (S-BERT similarity, factual-checker heuristics, and classifier outputs).

Q: Canary passed but production shows errors - why?
A: Verify routing, model variant mapping, and hardware differences. Production traffic distribution and longer tail inputs expose different failure modes; re-run failing prompts against production traffic capture.

Appendix: Example quick-check commands

- Run local eval smoke: python -m eval_harness.run --config eval_config/your-model.yaml --prompt-set summarization-small --limit 50
- Diff outputs: tools/diff_outputs.py --baseline run_12345 --candidate run_12346 --output s3://redwood-evals/incidents/run_12345_vs_12346.diff
